quired explanation as to why (1) the full details of the fourth and fifth plans and
of the eighth and particularly the ninth one have been given and (ii) the details
of the other plans, especially, of the last twenty-three rather twenty-two have
been altogether left out. From this passage it is clear beyond doubt that (a)
these thirty-two ground-plans are not intended to be independent and absolutely
separate plans, but (6) within a plan ofa larger numbor of plots, plans of smaller
number of plots may be marked and referred to by the technical epithets of
the latter, and that, therefore, the details of those plans which are not described
may be found out by merely multiplying the plans of which full details are
given, This would, further, explain why (i) the same number of twenty-five
deities are allocated to the plan of sixteen plots (i.e. Mahipitha) as well as
to the plan of twenty-five plots (i.c. Upapitha), and (ii) the same number of
forty-five deities are allocated to the plan of sixty-four plots (i.e. Chandita) and
to the plan of eighty-one plots (i.e. Parama-Sayika).
